issue.title: Bug: `test_k8s_disjoin_join.py` doesn't teardown iptables to original state

failure.body:
### Is it platform specific

generic

### Importance or Severity

Medium

### Description of the bug

When `kubesonic/test_k8s_join_disjoin.py` is run, there are some leftover config in `iptables` and `ip6tables`.

This could cause errors in `cacl/test_cacl_application.py` as it checks `iptables -S` and `ip6tables -S` for expected results (or similar tests that may use `iptables`/`ip6tables`).

Good to note `config reload` does reset the iptables, but is not guaranteed to run (and shouldn't be run just to teardown)

### Steps to Reproduce

On a clean DUT (config reloaded) run `iptables -S; ip6tables -S` OR `iptables-save; ip6tables-save`
Run `kubesonic/test_k8s_disjoin_join.py` test
run `iptables -S; ip6tables -S` OR `iptables-save; ip6tables-save` again
See difference

To see it causing test failures, run `kubesonic/test_k8s_disjoin_join.py` and `cacl/test_cacl_application.py` consecutively

### Actual Behavior and Expected Behavior

`kubesonic/test_k8s_disjoin_join.py` should teardown to leave iptables as it was originally

### Relevant log output

```shell
`cacl/test_cacl_application.py` failure when running it after kubesonic test:

E       Failed: Unexpected iptables rules: {'-A KUBE-FIREWALL -m comment --comment "kubernetes firewall for dropping marked packets" -m mark --mark 0x8000/0x8000 -j DROP', '-A INPUT -j KUBE-FIREWALL', '-N KUBE-FIREWALL', '-N KUBE-KUBELET-CANARY', '-A KUBE-FIREWALL ! -s <IP>/8 -d <IP>/8 -m comment --comment "block incoming localnet connections" -m conntrack ! --ctstate RELATED,ESTABLISHED,DNAT -j DROP', '-A OUTPUT -j KUBE-FIREWALL'}
```

### Approach
#### What is the motivation for this PR?
We noticed `kubesonic/test_k8s_join_disjoin.py` was causing failures in `cacl/test_cacl_application.py` as teardown didn't set `iptables`/`ip6tables` to original state.
#### How did you do it?
Save `iptables`/`ip6tables` config before the test, then restore it after the test
#### How did you verify/test it?
Ensure that `iptables`/`ip6tables` was the same before and after test, and it doesn't cause failures in `cacl/test_cacl_application.py` when run after
